title: Bucketing & KV Bloom - Midweek Sprint Scrub
content:
Context
- Quick mid-sprint sync focused on two related concerns: (1) smoothing batching jitter with a bucketing approach, (2) testing a compact Bloom-filter index on the KV cache to reduce false-KV lookups under high cardinality workloads.
- Motivation: last week's spike analysis showed a 40% increase in per-request kernel stalls during hot-path cache misses on long context sequences. Bucketing aims to make batching windows more predictable; Bloom reduces unnecessary GPU memops by filtering improbable keys.

Attendees (quick):
- Asha (lead) 
- Luis (kernel perf)
- Maya (KV cache + infra)
- Connor (e2e tests / perf harness)
- Priya (observability / rollout)

Minutes / Notes
1) Bucketing proposition (Asha + Luis)
- Idea: move from fixed micro-batch delay (x ms) to adaptive bucketing by expected sequence-length bins. Early prototype: three buckets (short <128 tokens, med 128-1024, long >1024). Each bucket has its own batch timer and capacity.
- Rationale: long queries are high variance and currently force the shared batching timer to either wait too long or fragment small requests. Separate timers let short requests gather quickly without being held for long-contending requests.
- Data: prototype sim on replayed trace (prod-sample-2028-05) shows median latency improvement: short bucket 22% down, p95 for short bucket down 15%. Long bucket throughput slightly reduced (~6%) but tail latency improved by redistributing resource pressure.
- Concerns: potential fragmentation under mixed workloads; we need fairness policy to avoid starving long sequences. Proposed fairness: token-weighted queue priority + soft-limits (if short queue length > X and long queue waiting > Y, force a merge window).

2) KV Bloom filter experiment (Maya)
- Prototype: compact Bloom per-shard in CPU memory (1 byte/entry equivalent hash footprint tuned for 2% false-positive rate). Query path checks Bloom before issuing GPU lookup.
- Replay run results: false positive rate observed ~2.4% (close to config), GPU lookup avoid rate ~27% on high-cardinality user-id traces, estimated GPU-memory-bandwidth saving 18% during peak.
- Downsides observed: additional CPU cycles for hashing (measured ~150ns per check) — negligible compared to GPU lookup cost on warm misses, but may add overhead on very short requests.
- Edge case: cache invalidation window causes transient false-negatives until Bloom refreshed — handled by rebuilding Bloom in slab with sliding epoch (see plan).

3) Integration discussion (Luis + Connor)
- Kernel change: need a fast branch in kernel dispatch for: bucket-id tag + bloom-skip flag to avoid scheduling GPU work. Add a tiny header word to request descriptor for these flags.
- Scheduler adaptation: when bloom-skip indicates no-GPU for a request, we fast-path to return cached token stream from CPU if available, otherwise mark as miss and possibly escalate.
- E2E harness: Connor to run combined bucketing+bloom replay with synthetic hybrid load (40% short, 40% med, 20% long) across 24-hour traces. Focus metrics: p50/p95 latency by bucket, GPU utilization, num GPU lookups avoided, and tail kernel stalls (blocked-on-memory).

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Luis: implement request-descriptor flag + kernel fast-check hook (branchless friendly). WIP PR target: draft by 2028-06-22.
- Maya: finalize Bloom rebuild sliding-epoch algorithm, add metrics (bloom_hit, bloom_fp, bloom_rebuild_time) to exporter. Target: 2028-06-20.
- Connor: prepare replay harness scenario and run first combined replay. Provide baseline vs current by 2028-06-23.
- Priya: dashboard tile for bucketing buckets with per-bucket tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, queue depths, and a Bloom skip ratio. Target: 2028-06-21.
- Asha: draft rollout plan (canary -> regional ramp -> global) with abort conditions and stakeholder list. Draft by 2028-06-24.

Open questions / Risks
- Fairness enforcement: how aggressive should token-weighted priority be before we compromise throughput?
- Bloom memory budget: current shard size constraints might require tuning; if shard_count increases, Bloom overhead might grow.
- Short-request CPU overhead: for sub-10ms requests, the extra hashing cost could be material. We should gate bloom checks behind minimal-request-size heuristic.
- Observability: we need to be able to correlate bloom-skip events with specific customer traces for debugging false positives; consider adding sampling of keys for traces.

Micro experiments (short-term, <7 days)
- A: Bucketing only (no Bloom) replay: validate p99 regressions on long-heavy traces. Owner: Luis.
- B: Bloom only (no bucketing): measure GPU lookup avoid ratio vs CPU overhead on short-heavy traces. Owner: Maya.
- C: Combined run with fairness knob set low/medium/high to measure throughput/latency tradeoffs. Owner: Connor.

Rollout & Safety checklist (initial canary)
- Canary cohort: non-paid internal clients + low-RPS test tenants; limit to 5% of traffic in region.
- Abort conditions: sustained 10% p50 regression for any bucket over 10 minutes, or increase in error-rate >0.5% absolute.
- Observability: enable debug sampling for 0.1% of requests to log pre/post kernel path.

Notes to self / quick reminders
- Remember to check prior kernel PR for request header layout (avoid collision with existing flags). Link: GH PR above.
- Need to sync with infra about memory overhead for Bloom replicas during rolling update (Maya).
- Consider incremental bucketization: start with 2 buckets (short / long) if 3-way fragmentation seems risky.

Meeting follow-ups / next sync
- Quick standup on Friday 09:30 PDT to review first replay numbers (Connor). If results look OK, begin kernel PR review cycle that day.
- Add a brief note to oncall handoff playbook for potential new failure mode: bloom-desync -> spurious misses.

Random brainstorming log (raw scribbles)
- Could we make Bloom tunable per-tenant? High-cardinality customers might opt-in.
- Use hardware accelerated hashing (crc32c) on CPU to reduce check latency on x86 AVX path.
- If short-requests see net negative impact from Bloom, flip to logic: if estimated end-to-end < threshold, skip bloom.

End of notes.

File status: draft — will iterate after Connor's replay runs and kernel prototype.
